Zero padding embeddings do not prevent GRU state updates: recurrent dynamics and biases can change hidden states during padding. Recommended implementation: extract each row’s nonpadding items in order, compact them into a right-padded tensor, compute lengths, then call `pack_padded_sequence(..., lengths.cpu(), batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)`. Exclude empty histories from packing and explicitly define their output. Start every independent user history with zero hidden state; never carry hidden state between unrelated users or batches. PyTorch supplies zeros when `h_0` is omitted. [Packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html), [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html).

Unpack with `pad_packed_sequence(..., batch_first=True, total_length=L)`, then scatter valid timestep outputs back to their original nonpadding positions so `log2feats` remains B×L×H and aligns with training targets. Unpacking restores original batch order when automatic sorting was used. Read the maximum nonpadding position—L−1 for nonempty strictly left-padded histories—never `count−1` in the original layout. For a unidirectional GRU, the packed final-layer `h_n` provides an equivalent final recurrent state before downstream transformations. [Unpacking documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence.html).

Recommended tests: compare identical histories under different padding widths; batched versus individual execution; batch permutations and changed neighboring users; repeated calls after unrelated batches; restored timestep outputs against unpadded references; empty/single-item histories; and saved predictor scores against training-model evaluation scores. Disable dropout with `eval()` for invariance checks. Suggested FP32 starting tolerances: `rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6`, adjusted using measured backend differences; bitwise equality is not guaranteed. Training, diagnostics and the embedded predictor must share packing, restoration and readout semantics. A claim that changes are unnecessary requires these tests to pass. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/numerical_accuracy.html).
